lede: Mountain Village Council meets Thursday to vote on a resolution setting the appreciation cap for deed-restricted affordable units — the fine print that determines whether those homes stay affordable for the next buyer, not just the first one. That same day, Telluride's P&Z holds a public hearing on new employee housing at the middle-high school site, and the BOCC sits Wednesday as the Housing Authority to work through regional affordable housing compliance. Ouray County's Planning Commission also holds three public hearings Wednesday, including a full repeal of Section 16 of its land use code — a significant rewrite worth paying attention to even from across the county line.
